MeHg.control: No government sets a methylmercury ML for any legume, pulse, peanut, or soy product in any jurisdiction; methylmercury maximum levels exist only for fish and seafood. Legumes and pulses are not a mercury-methylation matrix, and any mercury present is controlled by and bounded by the total-mercury ceiling for the subcategory. No methylmercury ML exists to look up.
MeHg.reference_method: MeHg by GC-ICP-MS / EN 16801 only on a lot whose total mercury approaches the tHg ceiling; legume/pulse methylmercury is characteristically < LOQ.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No regulatory MeHg ML for legume/pulse/peanut/soy products in any jurisdiction; methylmercury MLs are scoped to fish and seafood only. Total mercury is bounded by Israel FCS-2016 dried-legumes tHg 30 ug/kg.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; EU 2024/1987; Israel FCS-2016; MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011; Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; GSO 193; FDA; AU/NZ Sch 19; China GB 2762

Cr-VI.control: No government sets a hexavalent-chromium (Cr(VI)) maximum level for any legume, pulse, peanut, or soy product in any jurisdiction; Cr(VI) is never a published food ML in this domain. Total chromium IS regulated for part of this family: Hong Kong Cap 132V sets a total-Cr ML of 1000 ug/kg for pulses and China GB 2762 sets 1000 ug/kg for beans and legumes (these bind the dried-pulse and soy total-Cr cells), while no sovereign sets a total-Cr ML for peanuts. Chromium in this plant matrix is dominated by nutritionally-essential Cr(III), and Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in the organic-rich matrix; Cr(VI) is therefore bounded by the governing total-Cr ceiling. Firm control: reflex speciation - any total-Cr result >= 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails; Cr(VI) is never a panel number.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total-Cr screen by ICP-MS; on any result >= 100 ug/kg, Cr(VI) by EN 15192 / EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope-dilution; LOQ-level quantifiable Cr(VI) = fail.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No regulatory Cr(VI) ML for any legume/pulse/peanut/soy product in any jurisdiction. Total chromium is regulated for pulses and beans (Hong Kong Cap 132V pulses total-Cr 1000 ug/kg; China GB 2762 beans and legumes total-Cr 1000 ug/kg), which bind the dried-pulse and soy subcategories; no sovereign sets a total-Cr ML for peanuts. Cr(VI) is bounded by the governing total-Cr ceiling.
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; EU 2024/1987; Israel FCS-2016; MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011; Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; GSO 193; FDA; AU/NZ Sch 19; China GB 2762; Hong Kong Cap 132V

Sn.control: Every government tin maximum level in the register is scoped to canned / tin-coated product; tin migrates from tinplate, and that packaging-migration pathway is the contamination these MLs regulate. Dried legumes, pulses, peanuts, peanut butter, and soy products are not sold in tinplate, so that pathway is absent. Routed occurrence that has screened tin in these matrices reports it at or near non-detect (Roman-Ochoa 2021 measured bean tin at ~0.00 mg/kg against a sub-ppb LOD), i.e. dietary background rather than tinplate migration. Canned legume/pea products route to the canned-foods category and carry the tin ML there.
Sn.reference_method: Mandatory total-element screen by ICP-MS; tin is screened but not a binding numeric ceiling for non-canned product.
Sn.regulatory_basis: Tin MLs (EU/UK/GSO/IN 50000+ ug/kg; IN canned green peas / canned mushrooms) apply to canned product only; no non-canned legume/pulse Sn ML exists in any jurisdiction.
Sn.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; EU 2024/1987; Israel FCS-2016; MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011; Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; GSO 193; FDA; AU/NZ Sch 19; China GB 2762

Al.control: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum for plain legumes, pulses, peanuts, peanut butter, or soy products. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone numeric Al limit for this matrix; naturally present or additive-derived aluminium remains a surveillance and formulation-control issue governed by the additive rules of the markets of sale.
Al.reference_method: Screen total Al by ICP-MS and document any aluminium-containing additive or processing-aid use; investigate elevated results and comply with all additive rules in markets of sale.
